Review target: `1a6fc135..78aec45d`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

356	// ─── PropType — The Canonical Semantic Type Representation ────────────────────
357	
358	/// Semantic type of a prop. Rich enough to produce any output format.
359	/// Use match exhaustively — no `_` fallthrough in serializers.
360	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
361	pub enum PropType {
362	    // ── Primitives
363	    /// `string`.
364	    String,
365	    /// `number`.
366	    Number,
367	    /// `boolean`; a `true | false` union is collapsed into this.
368	    Boolean,
369	    /// `null`.
370	    Null,
371	    /// `undefined`.
372	    Undefined,
373	    /// `any`.
374	    Any,
375	    /// `never`.
376	    Never,
377	    /// `unknown`.
378	    Unknown,
379	    /// `void`.
380	    Void,
381	    /// `bigint`.
382	    BigInt,
383	
384	    // ── Literals
385	    /// A string literal type such as `"primary"`, holding the value without its quotes.
386	    StringLiteral(std::string::String),
387	    /// A number literal type such as `3`.
388	    NumberLiteral(f64),
389	    /// `true` or `false` as a type.
390	    BoolLiteral(bool),
391	    /// A bigint literal type such as `10n` or `-1n`.
392	    BigIntLiteral(BigIntValue),
393	    /// `typeof name` where the value `name` is declared `unique symbol`: a symbol type of its own, unlike `symbol`.
394	    UniqueSymbol {
395	        /// The name of the value declared `unique symbol` (`brand` in `declare const brand: unique symbol`).
396	        name: TypeName,
397	    },
398	    /// One member of an enum, as a type: `Size.Small` in `enum Size { Small = "small" }`. It is that member's value
399	    /// and keeps the enum's identity, which a plain literal loses.
400	    EnumMember {
401	        /// The enum's name as written (`Size`).
402	        enum_name: TypeName,
403	        /// The member's name (`Small`).
404	        member: TypeName,
405	        /// The member's value.
406	        value: EnumMemberValue,
407	    },
408	    /// A template literal type that stays a pattern, `` `${number}px` ``: its text pieces and `${…}` holes in order.
409	    /// A template whose holes are all finite literal unions is expanded to its strings instead.
410	    TemplateLiteral(Vec<TemplatePart>),
411	
412	    // ── Composites
413	    /// `A | B`: the members in declaration order.
414	    Union(Vec<PropType>),
415	    /// `A & B`: the members in declaration order.
416	    Intersection(Vec<PropType>),
417	    /// `T[]` or `Array<T>`: the element type.
418	    Array(Box<PropType>),
419	    /// `[A, B?, ...C[]]`: the elements in order, each with its optional, rest or variadic marker and its label. A
420	    /// spread of a tuple the resolver knows (`[A, ...Tail]`) is flattened into its elements, as TypeScript does.
421	    Tuple(Vec<TupleElement>),
422	    /// `readonly string[]` or `readonly [a, b]`: the array or tuple under the `readonly` operator.
423	    Readonly(Box<PropType>),
424	    /// An object type `{ a: string; b?: number }`: its members and index signatures, in declaration order.
425	    Object(Vec<ObjectField>),
426	    /// An object type with call or construct signatures that is not one plain function: overloads
427	    /// `{ (a: string): string; (a: number): number }`, a constructor `{ new (a: string): Date }`, or a function with
428	    /// properties `{ (): void; displayName?: string }`. A single call signature with nothing else is a [`Function`].
429	    ///
430	    /// [`Function`]: PropType::Function
431	    Callable {
432	        /// The call and construct signatures, in declaration order.
433	        signatures: Vec<CallSignature>,
434	        /// The properties and index signatures beside them, in declaration order.
435	        fields: Vec<ObjectField>,
436	    },
437	
438	    // ── Named reference (post-resolution)
439	    /// A reference to a type by name that the resolver kept rather than expanding (a type from a dependency that was
440	    /// not loaded, or one that is better shown as a name), with its type arguments.
441	    Named {
442	        /// The name of the referenced type.
443	        name: TypeName,
444	        /// Generic args, already resolved to PropType
445	        args: Vec<PropType>,
446	    },
447	    /// A reference back to a type whose expansion encloses it: the nested `Json` in
448	    /// `type Json = string | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json }`. Not a loss: the enclosing expansion is the type.
449	    Recursive {
450	        /// The name of the enclosing type.
451	        name: TypeName,
452	        /// Its type arguments as written at the reference.
453	        args: Vec<PropType>,
454	    },
455	    /// A type cut short at a depth or size limit, kept as its text. Unlike [`Opaque`] it is not a construct the
456	    /// resolver cannot read: it chose not to expand further. It counts in `degradedBy` as `truncated`.
457	    ///
458	    /// [`Opaque`]: PropType::Opaque
459	    Truncated {
460	        /// The type's text where it was cut: its name, or how the checker prints it.
461	        text: std::string::String,
462	        /// Which limit cut it.
463	        limit: TruncationLimit,
464	    },
465	
466	    // ── React-specific terminals
467	    /// React's `ReactNode`. `ReactElement` and `JSX.Element`, which are narrower, stay

469	    ReactNode,

471	    CssProperties,
472	    /// A function type: callbacks, render props and event handlers alike (`(value: number) => ReactNode`).
473	    Function {
474	        /// The function's own type parameters: `T` in `<T>(item: T) => ReactNode`.
475	        type_params: Vec<std::string::String>,
476	        /// The parameters in order.
477	        params: Vec<FunctionParam>,
478	        /// What the function returns, as written.
479	        return_type: Box<PropType>,
480	    },
481	    /// `Ref<T>`, `RefObject<T>`, `ForwardedRef<T>` and the other ref types React declares.
482	    Ref {
483	        /// The React type as written, without a `React.` prefix: `RefObject`, `ForwardedRef`, `RefCallback`.
484	        name: std::string::String,
485	        /// Inner element type if known
486	        element: Option<std::string::String>,
487	    },
488	    /// React.ElementType — component can render as any element
489	    /// Used for: `as?: ElementType`, `component?: ElementType`
490	    ElementType,
491	
492	    // ── HTML attribute inheritance
493	    /// All attributes of an HTML element, minus omitted keys.
494	    /// Produced when we see ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'> etc.
495	    HtmlAttributes {
496	        /// The HTML element whose attributes are inherited: `button` in `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>`.
497	        element: std::string::String,
498	        /// Attribute names left out of the element's set.
499	        omitted: Vec<std::string::String>,
500	    },
501	
502	    // ── Variant systems (statically resolved)
503	    /// Result of CvaVariantPropsHandler — the wrapper is fully dissolved.
504	    /// Each member is a string literal value.
505	    LiteralUnion {
506	        /// The string literal values, in declaration order.
507	        members: Vec<std::string::String>,
508	        /// true if this prop has a defaultVariant
509	        has_default: bool,
510	    },
511	
512	    // ── Known opaque patterns (cannot/should not be expanded)
513	    /// MUI SxProps, SystemStyleObject etc. — complex, not user-facing props
514	    SxProps,
515	
516	    // ── Unresolvable — graceful degradation
517	    /// A type the resolver gave up on, kept as written with the reason. Every one comes with a diagnostic that
518	    /// explains why (see [`OpaqueDetail`]).
519	    Opaque(OpaqueDetail),
520	}

522	/// The private payload of `PropType::Opaque`. Fields are unreachable from
523	/// outside this module — the only ways to build one are `give_up` (pushes
524	/// the diagnostic that explains the degradation, then builds the value) and
525	/// `new` (for the one documented exception: `known.rs`, which has no
526	/// diagnostics channel of its own and pushes its own diagnostic separately
527	/// via `known::push_known_opaque_diagnostic` — see that function's doc
528	/// comment). Read the payload back through `raw()`/`reason()`.
529	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
530	pub struct OpaqueDetail {
531	    raw: std::string::String,
532	    reason: OpaqueReason,
533	}
534	
535	impl OpaqueDetail {
536	    #[allow(clippy::new_ret_no_self)]
537	    pub(crate) fn new(raw: impl Into<std::string::String>, reason: OpaqueReason) -> PropType {
538	        PropType::Opaque(OpaqueDetail { raw: raw.into(), reason })
539	    }
540	
541	    /// The sanctioned "give up and record why" constructor — pushes
542	    /// `diagnostic` onto `state` before building the value, so a resolver
543	    /// call site that reaches for this can't forget to explain the
544	    /// degradation the way the old bare `PropType::Opaque { .. }` literal let
545	    /// call sites do.
546	    pub(crate) fn give_up(
547	        state: &mut ResolveState,
548	        raw: impl Into<std::string::String>,
549	        reason: OpaqueReason,
550	        diagnostic: Diagnostic,
551	    ) -> PropType {
552	        state.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
553	        #[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods, reason = "the diagnostic is pushed on the line above")]
554	        Self::new(raw, reason)
